# Rust execution slicing

A Rust slice is not a file quota or a crate layer. It is the smallest coherent increment that creates integrated feedback.

For each slice:

- identify the exact crates, modules, public contracts, generated artifacts, features, targets, and work units required for the touchpoint;
- keep one accountable integration owner;
- define the candidate/validation cohort and exact assertions;
- choose a touchpoint such as a CLI operation, API exchange, protocol trace, downstream consumer test, packaged-crate exercise, migration rehearsal, or measured benchmark;
- name temporary mocks, adapters, fixtures, feature flags, generated bindings, or compatibility shims and their disposition;
- include rollback, complete-forward, containment, or safe abandonment behavior;
- preserve repository commands and effect authority.

A foundation-first slice is acceptable only when a vertical touchpoint would be misleading, the foundation retires a named feasibility or safety risk, it has its own inspectable result, and the next integrated slice is named.
